notes: JR, Shinkansen, Tokyo Metro and Toei lines are curated (scripts/tokyo); private railways, third-sector lines, monorails, AGT and trams are imported from OpenStreetMap route relations (cities/tokyo). Geometry and station positions © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL (simplified ~15 m), clipped to lng 139.0-140.4 / lat 35.2-36.2 (lines are truncated at that box). Interchanges are merged when stations share a name (Japanese or English) within ~400-450 m; differently named transfer stations (Seibu-Shinjuku / Shinjuku, Keisei-Ueno / Ueno, Tokyo Skytree / Oshiage) stay separate. Segment years are first-opening years of each line, rounded; private-railway branches carry their line's first year. Private lines follow the operators' station-number prefixes, so branches sharing a prefix (Keikyu KK, Keisei KS, Keio KO, Sotetsu SO, Seibu SI) are drawn as branches of one line where OSM groups them that way. Upcoming JR / subway projects: Namboku Shinagawa branch and Yurakucho Toyosu-Sumiyoshi extension (construction, mid-2030s, shown as 2035), JR Haneda Airport Access Line East route (construction, FY2031) and Rinkai route (planned), Tokyo Rinkai Subway (planned), Oedo Hikarigaoka-Oizumi-gakuenmachi extension (planned). Upcoming private-railway projects: Shin-Kuko (Kamakama) Line phase 1 (approved, early 2040s), Tama Monorail Kamikitadai-Hakonegasaki (approved, mid-2030s) and Tama Center-Machida (planned), Tsukuba Express Akihabara-Tokyo (planned), Yokohama Blue Line Azamino-Shin-Yurigaoka (planned), Saitama Railway Urawa-Misono-Iwatsuki (planned, April 2041), Odakyu Tama Line Karakida-Sagamihara-Kamimizo (planned). Their stations and alignments are approximate (approx) and names provisional. Not included: Hokuriku Shinkansen, limited-express-only services, Kanto Railway, Shibayama Railway, Izu-Hakone and Hakone Tozan, Kominato and Isumi, Disney Resort Line.
